Name: -1_maiden_spoon_flower_rice
Representative_Docs:
['The mountain is harsh and the water is harsh, words cannot be spoken, a deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river, and when I lose someone, I lose a part of myself too.  
When others lose someone, I lose someone as well. How could I not serve my husband faithfully despite this harsh fate?  
My poor husband, do not go—who will raise our young children? What sin do they bear in their youth? I just gaze up at the sky,  
thinking of my husband. When I think about it, I realized what my husband’s love truly was, but before I could fully understand, you passed away.  
How can I possibly raise this young, immature child alone? Ah, my grief…  
In this neighborhood alley, I wonder if my husband is here. Every day, whenever the sun rises, I think of my husband; even when looking at the moon, I think of him.  
I waited anxiously, hoping my husband would come home, but he has gone beyond this world. The cruel attachment remains even as I try to forget; no matter how much I steel my heart,  
your image from yesterday and today still appears vividly in my eyes.  
How could you leave me alone and go where you went?  
My in-laws complain morning and evening, my sister-in-law is troublesome, my brother-in-law is frantic,  
I carefully watch my behavior while trusting only my husband. With a single heart, I vowed to love you always,  
but why did you leave me and go beyond this world? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear.  
If I had known you were going to leave me, I would have built a fortress at the edge of the world where you went,  
If I had known it would come to this, I would have called a shaman to perform rites and exorcisms, to try to save you.  
I never imagined you would go beyond this world. They say that place beyond is better than this life; if I had known,  
every morning and evening I would have drawn holy water and prayed with my hands clasped, asking my husband not to die.  
Why did you leave me so heartlessly? Even today, I think of you. On the cold winds of winter’s end and the snow-filled solstice,  
the west winds of Bukcheongsan blow fiercely downward. That harsh winter has passed, and spring has come.  
The nightingale sings lightly and deeply, crying, and the mountains and trees—even dead wood—revive, sprouting leaves and flowers,  
but when will my departed husband come? Without a word, you torment me so.  
It is frustrating and painful; I cannot speak of it before me. A deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river.  
Coal, anthracite, bituminous coal, straw coal, bear’s fat—when burning, they produce smoke and steam, but my longing for my husband burns without any smoke or steam, only sorrow flows quietly like a droplet.  
Who understands this bruised liver? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, so dear, oh, my dear.', "In Muan land, the golden maiden  
desired to be married.  
Soon after getting married,  
in the room where water liquor was made,  
she was told to spend the night.  
They lit a big charcoal fire,  
used the jade lamp for light,  
hung it over the bed,  
and placed a reed mat.  
They laid down eastward, westward,  
and seeing the silk bundles left,  
they placed a mat on the floor,  
and after a short sleep,  
whispered secretly,  
looking out at some city,  
and conspired to kill.  
Whispering secretly, again,  
looking out at some city,  
and conspired to kill.  
Tomorrow at the market, at Muan market,  
there will be a special event for five don coins.  
With soybean paste soup like poison,  
stirred up and placed on the table,  
the water liquor single-layer blouse,  
worn very nicely and tightly,  
the water liquor black skirt,  
worn very nicely and tightly.  
At the mat stone floral seat,  
who would pair up and spread it?  
With the hair parted in two,  
swept beyond the comb lines,  
after taking a sip,  
all the four limbs loosen up.  
After two sips,  
the six thousand horses all collapse.  
After three sips,  
off they go and get tipsy.  
An older schoolmate who went to Seoul,  
like the Oe family’s elder,  
kicks off the Yangje side by foot,  
complaining about married life being tough.  
Why would she take a nap?  
In the inner chamber, parents say,  
she is the golden maiden, she is hers.  
Like a morning star, the chamber pot’s dignity,  
she is the golden maiden, she is hers.  
Half open the main hall door,  
tell mother to leave,  
tell father to leave,  
if the groom's mother-in-law knows,  
what kind of responsibility would she take?  
Plow the front field to buy servants,  
plow the back field to buy hired workers,  
manage the treatment of injuries well,  
an illness that lasts three or four days  
was cured in one day.  
After three or four days of coming to see,  
it had turned into a wormwood field.  
Alas, hurrah!", "Aga aga, Minul aga,  
They say it's a field, but it's all tangled up.  
Every little corner is covered with sesame,  
Seaweed is gathered on the hills.  
Each head is tied tightly,  
One bundle, two bundles,  
Even if you gather three bundles a day,  
All the officials have come and gone.  
But no one like Yone (a righteous man) appears.  
Aga aga, Minul aga,  
Step back, this path—  
They say it’s a matter of work.  
Looking for the right time and season,  
What is given as food  
Is three-year-old barley rice,  
Stuck to the bowl’s edge.  
What is given as the sauce  
Is three-year-old dinggi jang (fermented sauce).  
The plates are covered in dirt,  
And the spoons are just thrown away  
Ten or five ri (Korean miles) off,  
Twelve widths of cloth,  
One width torn into a cone hat,  
Eleven widths packed in a basket.  
Entering the bamboo grove,  
Leaning on the old fence,  
Mother and father, please receive my bow,  
I take my leave and step back.  
One watering turn passes, over a hundred seeds tremble,  
Two watering turns pass, all the dry corn trembles,  
Three watering turns and  
My husband who has gone to Seoul  
Holds a brush in his mouth,  
A book tucked at his side.  
My dear, my beloved,  
I am going, please don’t go.  
May my parents live a thousand years and ten thousand years,  
Leaving you behind, I find my way back to the temple.  
Master Jung, Master Jung,  
Is the place for poetry begging?  
Going to the place for poetry begging,  
Mother, please give a little alms.  
Though you do not give alms,  
My child’s face shows through,  
Like a newborn child—  
Not that word, please give a little more,  
Oh child, please give alms,  
Glutinous rice and millets are all done,  
Give a hand of millet alms,  
The bottomless sack receives the alms.  
Getting up, the fly falls,  
I slap with my hands in rejection.  
I slap with the gourd too,  
Filling a whole basket with that guy.  
Waiting for Aunt’s husband,  
He comes making steamed rice dishes,  
The bottomless sack, did you come for alms?  
Giving a fool’s gift, then leaving,  
As time passes and I come again,  
The household is ruined,  
In front of father-in-law’s rice storage,  
Pumpkin flowers are in abundance,  
In front of mother-in-law’s rice storage,  
Only withered flowers have bloomed.  
In front of Dongshi’s rice storage,  
Poison flowers bloom profusely,  
In front of sister-in-law’s rice storage,  
Cherry blossoms bloom profusely.  
On the husband’s mother’s place,  
Full blooms of cabbage flowers,  
Cabbage, oh cabbage,  
Looking at me, you bloom fully.  
Why do you bloom so fully?  
With that sound, the cabbage flower split apart,  
And entered the mountain alive."]

Name: 0_wedding_bride_marriage_joyful
Representative_Docs:
['When youthful blood flows through the veins  
Love and wine often elevate,  
When the fire of love ignites the heart,  
Everyone may well be joyful.  
We then want to ride off,  
And let the festive song resound,  
And raise it in honor  
Of bride and groom. b.

We first dedicate the song  
To the honor of the groom,  
And wish that you will long  
Rejoice in the blessing of love.  
May your bride soon crown your wish,  
At least within the year,  
Then playfully on your lap a son—  
This is the wish of the circle of friends. b.

We, dear bride, begin to sing;  
We dedicate our song to you,  
And wish that no tear of sadness  
Ever runs down your cheeks;  
If our desire is crowned,  
Then may it be decreed for you,  
That the spouse always shows such love  
As on the first night in bed. b.

We all wish, youthful couple,  
You the greatest happiness on earth,  
May you be spared from each other  
Many years in pure love.', 'Now let Bagchus be praised,  
The cup in hand,  
Come, friends! let us sing, let us rejoice,  
In this ecstatic state;  
Now pour the noble grape juice,  
In pure crystal clear,  
Long live this noble wedding treasure,  
Long live, long live the Wine! (repeat)  
Wine makes heart and mind joyful;  
Gives us a cheerful mood,  
Brings joy to a wedding meal,  
And spices the abundance;  

Where Wine is lacking, it is cold and stiff;  
There can be no life,  
So let Bagchus remain honored.  
Long live, long live the Wine! (repeat)  
Rejoice, friends, and sound it all around;  
Sing Bagchus gladly in honor,  
Everyone raises the glass to the mouth,  
So that everyone takes the turn;  
Who honors Bagchus, who serves Bagchus,  
May be at a wedding,  
Long live, he is the friend of us all,  
Long live, long live the Wine! (repeat)', 'The day of the joyous celebration is here,  
The joy sounds loudly,  
In honor of this worthy couple,  
Adorned with silver crowns.  
Raise your song, o friends!  
Sing merrily, again and again,  
So that your cheerful festivity  
Sounds in honor of the Silver Pair. (repeat)  

The groom, esteemed for his virtue,  
As well as his worthy bride,  
They receive our best wishes,  
With lively accompaniment;  
Yes, certainly upon the generous reception,  
They are now welcome here,  
As they proudly appear once again  
As bride and groom. (repeat)  

How many honest and virtuous pledges  
Adorn your marriage crown,  
And contribute to the joy of the bond,  
Your marriage as a reward;  

Their grateful heart is devoted to you,  
So noble for your virtue,  
Behold how that heart is now delighted,  
And rejoices in your happiness. (repeat)  

May you both live long, blessed with well-being,  
Finding gentle cause for joy,  
Let this joyous celebration be for you a symbol,  
Of the marriage’s flower garden;  
Proceed together with a clear mind,  
To many more years,  
And celebrate once the Golden wedding,  
As joyfully as this hour. (repeat)  

O marital love! O highest joy,  
That delights the human heart,  
O friendship! pure soul’s delight,  
To you both our song honors;  
Weave mirth and palm into a victory crown,  
Share your influence with us,  
For you resound the happiest tone,  
At the universal hurrah! (repeat)']

Name: 1_fate_sorrow_life daughter_mother mother
Representative_Docs:
['Mother, mother, our mother  
Why did you bring me out?  
You must have been strong when you carried me,  
But you left me in this village.  
I cannot live by farming.  
Mother, mother, please take me away.  
I cannot live like this.  
Oh dear, oh dear, this is my fate.  

Looking at the mountains,  
Looking at these mountains,  
Feelings I never had arise naturally.  
Some people have good fate,  
Proud of their luck, proud of their wealth.  
Great houses in a high, wide mansion,  
Living well with wealth and honor.  

Where did I go wrong?  
Because I was born unlucky,  
My fate turned out this way.  
What spirit could know my heart?  
What earth could know my heart?  
What God could know my heart?  
I cannot live like this.  

Mother, mother, our mother,  
Please take me away.  
I cannot live even among the mountains.  
Take me somewhere good.  

- Sighing sound  
>', "Fate, fate, my fate  
When my mother and father were alive,  
What did they eat, and how did I grow up?  
I couldn't live well in this cruel world.  
Leaving the mainland and all its hardships behind, where does one go?  
Mother, mother, my mother,  
When I was born, and also when others are born,  
Though men and women come into this world,  
What kind of destiny is so harsh?  
Living life,  
Though I give birth to sons and daughters,  
Unable to raise them properly,  
There is endless lamentation about fate.  
Child, endure, this is my destiny.  
If I die, I am still young,  
If I live, it is full of hardship.  
Children, when you were born,  
After ten months in the womb,  
I lay down in the real place,  
And you lay down in the empty place.  
Though I fed you three meals a day,  
What has appeared from that?  
Such is the world.  
When I lived in this world,  
There was only a small fire in the yard,  
If it burns only on the outside, is that the person?  
If it burns only inside, is that not the person?  
Look at life in this world.  
The fire in my heart,  
Should I try burning it like the fire on Namsan?  

– Heunggeul sound", 'At sixteen, I married,
The year I first wore a gat, I lost my husband,
Thought I would die, oh youth,
Wanted to live, but hardship awaits.
Clinging to the pillar of the veranda, I turned around,
Stepping outside the main gate,
Out of nowhere, a wild goose
Brings news of my beloved.
On the long, long night of the winter solstice,
As I sit, sleep does not come,
As I lie down, my love does not appear.
After crying all night long,
My sorrow has deepened.
The river of tears is indeed a river,
A pair of ducks, a pair of geese,
Two pairs, four of them, have come flying.
The green ones are willows,
The yellow ones are orioles,
The golden orioles,
Wearing armor like gold,
Go to find my love in the Tumen River.
Do not recklessly shoot,
I lost my love like this,
Wandering in search of him.
Looking up, there is a cliff,
Looking down, barren land.
A bent old general,
Unable to withstand the harsh gale,
Only dances wildly.
Climbing the mountain, eating wild plants,
Turning back, it is a famous mountain.
Plucking flowers to place on my head,
Tearing off leaves to play the zither,
Breaking pine branches to use as a cane,
Climbing the mountain to enjoy the scenery,
Passersby,
See only me and cannot leave.
Only when I climb the hill behind,
Do I think of my beloved,
On the green grass leaves, I realize,
The dew has all arrived.']

Name: 2_law mother_mother law_daughter law_grandmother
Representative_Docs:
['In March, at Jinjin Sea, the maiden heads to the Jiseon field,  
Should she carry one bundle or two bundles?  
Having carried three bundles, a letter arrives, a letter arrives,  
A letter comes from her parental home. She takes it with one hand,  
Receiving it with both hands, it’s a letter announcing her mother’s death.  
Father, father, a letter arrived about our mother’s passing.  
“Put on your hemp clothes and go,” says the mother-in-law,  
“Mother died, there’s a letter.” The mother-in-law says,  
“Have some food before you go.”  
Asking her husband,  
“If you don’t go, who else will?”  
Taking off her raincoat and holding it close,  
Letting down her hair and walking slowly,  
Taking off her shoes, holding them in her hand,  
Turning once, the crows cawed loudly,  
Turning again, the sound of the threshing board echoed,  
Turning once more, the wailing resounded,  
Entering the courtyard of her parental home, the sound of street vendors echoed.  
Eldest sister-in-law among nine siblings,  
“Open the gate a little,”  
“You should push them away; if you keep messing, you came here,”  
“I want to see my parents’ faces once more.”  
Second sister-in-law among nine siblings,  
“Open the gate a little,”  
“You should stop causing trouble; you came here,”  
“I want to see my parents’ faces once more.”  
Youngest sister-in-law among nine siblings,  
“Open the gate a little,”  
“Open the gate and go inside,  
Walk around the room once,  
The room is wide and empty, like an empty banquet hall.”  
Eldest sister-in-law among nine siblings,  
“If you clear the salt field,  
You’ll eat and I’ll eat too.”  
“There’s some leftover purge water,  
You get your share, I get mine.”  
“When the scorched rice is done,  
You have yours, I have mine.”', 'Three days after marriage, my sister-in-law, who picks cherries, urges me to weed the baby field.  
Look at the behavior of my mother-in-law.  
She washed her feet with cold water and urges me to weed the field.  
After weeding the first hill, then the second and third hills,  
it is almost lunchtime. As I arrive to have lunch,  
the sharp-tongued mother-in-law stirs her cold water feet.  
"Yesterday you came, my dear daughter-in-law, and today again, my dear daughter-in-law,  
what kind of work is this, coming only for lunch?"  
Hearing that voice, I was so overwhelmed that I couldn’t speak.  
Returning to my room, I tore seven pieces of cloth.  
I used two pieces to make a patchwork pouch, three pieces to make a bag,  
and one piece to make a simple sash, cutting and cutting,  
cutting my hair to look like a monk.  
I was going, but my husband said to go.  
He said he would ride a horse and go to the Seonbun family.  
Wearing half a plain sleeve, I turned around the side door.  
My husband said, "Dear, Shinjung family,  
don’t start any trouble with people.  
Dear, wearing half a plain sleeve,  
turn around the side door."  
At the end of his words, I suddenly grabbed his hand fiercely,  
trembling all over. "What’s wrong with you?  
What’s the matter with you, who usually wears a silk brocade waist bag?  
Why suddenly shave your head, who used to wear a golden hairpin and chop its hair?  
Why wear straw shoes over your worn shoes?  
Let’s go, let’s go back home."  
"I can’t go, I can’t go.  
Your parents' family is good, but I’m different, I have to go."  
Returning home, I asked my mother, "Where did he go?"  
"Since you left, he went away." The words made me so overwhelmed.  
Inside the three-foot coffin, inside the coffin, I cut my neck and died. / Sop'al', 'Mother, mother, why did my mother send me out?
There was no place to plant me, so why was I planted here?
After weeding one row, then two rows,
and two and a half rows in the Jangcheon field,
it was time for lunch.
Returning home,
I ate white porridge, then red bean porridge,
and at the end of the shelf in front of the ancestral tablet,
I wondered whether to eat or not eat that meal.
At that, the neighboring grandmother, hearing this,
said, "Chun-a, Chun-a, Okdang Chun-a, if that child belongs to the house, isn’t there a home?
If that is rice, isn’t there rice?"
Cutting and cutting off the hair, going to the temple,
hearing the neighbor’s grandmother’s words, I tore twelve pieces of cloth,
hung them up loosely, tore one piece to gather nuts,
two pieces to make a bag, and from the remaining cloth made a satin robe to wear.
Climbing the hill behind the village, the monk’s shoe strap broke,
so I asked for directions: "Please give me the way, the back gate, that way, please give me the way."
Looking along one side of the main gate, the young monk was sleeping,
the old monk did not answer, but there was also an old servant,
so I woke the young monk and told him,
"Please tie my hair, please tie my hair,
Please tie my hair tight,
If you tie it tight, at least say your name and surname."
After tying my hair into one headpiece,
the front of my hair was all wet.
After tying two bundles of hair, the front got wet with rain.
Wearing the monk’s robe, holding the wooden fish and rosary beads in my hand,
I crossed over and set out on a large road,
wearing a sky-like hat, riding a dragon-like horse,
coming along smoothly and nicely.
A person I did not know entered and stood still,
“Why? Why?”
My body felt as heavy as a thousand pounds.
“Why, monk’s robe? Why?”
"Why is this my wooden fish rosary like fire?"
Taking off the monk’s robe, I sat up, I sat up,
sat up on the embankment, sat up on the water fork embankment,
"Hurry and go, hurry and go, you must leave.
The three years of study, the studying for three years, now I am leaving after three years.
Running here and there, I can’t even run in the water."
Arriving at the gate in front of the house, the stone seat was wet,
this is the grace of the parents,
entered the room, as if asleep, gone.']

Name: 4_bride_wedding_bridesmaids_getting married
Representative_Docs:
['1.

Klaartje was leaning over her front door,  
Japik, her neighbor, was standing there talking to her; –  
Was it about calves, was it about cows,  
Was it about a wedding or the fair?…  
I stood a bit far away, and they spoke softly;  
But she shook her head no,  
And she called out: ‘Would you stop that!’  
And she laughed with him.  

2.

I swear it was Easter time!… The nightingale sang,  
When I saw a bridal couple entering the church;  
Everyone gave smiles, everyone gave greetings…  
What was the pastor asking the bride?  
I stood a bit far away, and he preached softly;  
But she nodded yes,  
And she looked down,  
And she cried afterward.', 'There was recently a sweet Bride,  
Hail to the Bride!  
She looked, oh! so lovely  
Boys, boys, boys, what a sweet Bride!

She sat next to her Groom,  
Hail, Groom, hail!  
And friends and maids all around,  
Boys, boys, boys, what a Groom!

Everyone was cheerful and joyful,  
Yes, truly joyful!  
And laughed and sang out of pure joy,  
Singing, singing, singing yes, out of pure joy!

Oh, they danced around,  
Oh yes, around,  
And stayed until the morning hour.  
Certainly, certainly, certainly, until the morning hour.

And they drank many a glass,  
Yes, many a glass!  
It was as if Bacchus himself was the pourer,  
Bacchus, Bacchus, Bacchus was the pourer.

But what did the sweet Couple do?  
What did the Couple do?  
They sat picking on each other,  
Hahaha, hahaha, hahaha, well well, that sweet Couple!

And what did the Groom do then?  
What did he do then?  
Well, he gave his Bride a kiss,  
Hahaha, hahaha, hahaha, yes, that’s what he did then.

But does this naughty existence not demand revenge?  
Yes, it demands revenge!', 'I know a certain bird, a hoopoe by name, who wants to get married: he will marry a jay. Many guests were invited to that merry wedding, from various birds, both large and small. The golden-headed bunting was the best man, and the joyful lark invited the guests to the wedding. The quail was the bridesmaid, the wreath fairy, leading the maiden jay, the bride, to the ceremony. The raven officiated, the hawk stood as a witness, forbidding any friends to be present. The crow was the cook, preparing their lunch: everyone could see how he blackened himself. The nightingale played music after the meal, and all the guests danced. The jay became tired and went to sleep, while the lively magpie made her bed. The wedding was completed, I end this song, at which I was also present and watched it. It happened that year and still happens today: when the hoopoe comes to the jay, the wedding is done.']

Name: 23_flowers bloom_flowers_blossoms_flower
Representative_Docs:
["Look at me, just look at me  
Just take a little look at me  
Like seeing a flower in the last month of winter  
Just take a little look at me  

I know you like the bright moon on a clear night  
But do you know me  
Like dark, dense reeds?  
If you cared for me as much as I do for you  
Even a thousand miles of thorny brambles, I’d walk barefoot  

On days when the sun sets and fades away  
Where do you go, wearing your outer clothes?  
If you're going to a mistress's house  
Watch me die before you go  

The mistress’s house is a flower garden  
But my house is a pond  
Flowers and butterflies are only for one spring season  
But the goldfish by the pond live through all four seasons  

Oh, how wonderful, oh, how fine  
No, I cannot stay like this", "The leaves bloom as Cheongsan, and the flowers bloom as Hwasan.  
My body goes nowhere but Jeolgol.  
Though the old sheep is not sorrowful, the old ox is indeed sorrowful.  
Myeongsashimri Hae-danghwa, do not be sorrowful because your flowers are falling.  
Did I want to lose? I must always be unwavering; I have lost.  

(Sewing song?)  
In the world or at Mingyeong, pouring plum blossom syrup into a jade cup,  
Even if I quilt a lambskin jacket sleeve or a top,  
My beloved neither comes nor sleeps, and the rooster crows loudly.  
Neither holy water nor shamans' prayers help.  
No need for five layers of silk satin, nor five layers of fine silk.  
I embrace the eternal farewell and go forth.", 'Dried pollack travels a thousand miles, wood travels a thousand miles  
The blooming garden is like a flourishing maiden  
Hair like blossoms hanging down, washed in the water of the Milky Way  
With a red ribbon as a fashion statement, from the waist of Baekdu Mountain to the waist of Geumgang Mountain  
Oh youth, oh bright youth, from the waist of a grown child  
At seventeen, eighteen, nineteen years old  
Applying red lipstick and forehead decoration, all spent in married life  
Flowers bloom and buds form, leaves sprout as youth is seen  
When the flowers fall, leaves also wither, in the cold midwinter and early winter wind  
When white snowflakes fly, fallen leaves drop suddenly  
Even with hoary white hair, youth is gone, and even the prime of life grows old  
When white snow falls over the western mountains, all old white hair is fully aged']

Name: 24_maiden_mistress_bride_beauty

['You ruled over a gentle brother,

Afterwards, you got the woman  
Who had an elbow on her shoulder,  
Who had arsenic teeth,  
With dull eyes in exchange.  
She does not feel like walking,  
Sitting on the bed without sparks,

Taken along with me:  
I know a dull girl,  
I see that snub-nosed girl,  
A dull girl with long hair,  
A lazy girl with wide locks,  
A belt fluid on her thigh.', 'Dear Mistress of dominion,  
Do you see that maiden on the IJ,  
In the first days of her life,  
Whom your mother bore,  
Blushing from cakes, and the stroke  
Of that lovely smile?  

What worries does she have?  
Mind works, hands go.  
Her eyes are busy.  
Throat and lips are restless.  
Can a youth, fresh with years,  
Stand against so much effort?

See that thumb, with golden threads  
Grinding costly fabrics:  
Fingers wield pen, pencil:  
Knuckles tickle the many.  

See once, that tender little mouth,  
With the nuts, up and down:  
The eye glues itself to the letters:  
Mind submerged in the rhyme:  
Tongue bends in the sound  
Of the Roman and the French.', 'A young virgin girl,  
A little bird with flaxen hair,  
You think of beauty without a husband,  
A white girl without a husband,

You think of bashful men without a husband.  
You are not beautiful without a husband,

Nor a pure boy without a husband,  
You are strange without a husband,  
A thief without a husband,

And old maids to envy.  
Are you not pure without a boy,  
Are you not a white bride either,  
Are you not beautiful at all,  
Or are you clever in some way?"']

Name: 31_rooster_crows_pillow_grandmother
Representative_Docs:

washed in water and plucked off, fluttering here and there,  
stirring me this way and that, am I a fighting rooster or a lost soul?  
Crying by day, crying by night.", 'The evening comes late,  
The rooster sings at dawn,  
May we be home by dawn.  
At dusk to father-in-law’s yard,  
At dark to mother-in-law’s yard,  
To the white village between.  
How do I recognize father-in-law’s yard?  
The upset cow moos,  
The ugly dog barks,  
The cheerful rooster crows,  
Because I recognize father-in-law’s yard,  
I remember mother-in-law’s yard.', 'When it’s a bit chilly, come into my arms,  
When the bamboo fence is tall, lean on my arms.  
With mandarin ducks, a golden hairpin, and a pine bamboo fence placed by the pillow,

Looking up, there’s a conch shell tray; looking down, a patterned straw mat.  
On the patterned straw mat in the sleeping room’s floor—what’s going on?  
Why is there a pillow in the rice measuring box where you used to tuck your head?  
Why are there iron chains on the handcuffs you used to wear?  
Why is there a red hemp jeogori over the clothes you wore?  
Why is there a straw shoe for the sharp pointed shoes you used to wear?  
Oh, let’s live on with the sound of the side drum and the clatter of the earthenware jar.  
Oh, how good it is—this feeling I can’t deny.  
When is sleep ever at ease? Just now, I was blowing on it for warmth.  
Oh, this feeling—I cannot deny it.

— When playing, lamenting about fate?']
